title: EU Vinted action shows a second-hand marketplace converting complaint pressure into implemented price, refund, identity, and review controls
source_unit: European Commission Consumer Protection Cooperation Network dialogue with Vinted
geography: European Union and European Economic Area consumer-facing Vinted websites and mobile apps

observations.period: December 2021 dialogue through Commission follow-up current at 2026 source retrieval

denominator.unit: EU/EEA Vinted consumers and sellers; no affected-consumer count disclosed

implemented_total_price.value: Vinted modified its website and app to inform consumers upfront about the total price, including the automatically added buyer-protection fee

misleading_free_ads.value: Vinted removed misleading advertisements creating the impression that purchases were free of charges

buyer_protection_fee_issue.value: automatic buyer-protection fee addition at checkout without upfront information was addressed
buyer_protection_fee_issue.unit: documented complaint issue and platform response

mechanism.value: Complaint-backed intervention can convert a hidden service charge into an upfront total-price signal before a second-hand purchase is committed

observations.method: European Commission page reporting changes Vinted made following dialogue with the CPC Network and national consumer authorities; the page distinguishes implemented changes from unresolved requests.
observations.uncertainty: The official page does not quantify the number of complaints, affected buyers, fee amounts, completed refunds, or whether clearer prices changed purchase behavior or seller income.
observations.subgroup: Consumers buying and sellers listing second-hand goods on Vinted versions directed to EU/EEA users.
observations.counterinterpretation: Upfront disclosure can improve informed choice without reducing the underlying fee or making second-hand goods more affordable; consumers may still accept the charge for convenience or protection.

observations.period: Vinted CPC implementation; failed delivery, counterfeit, identity, and review controls

denominator.unit: EU/EEA Vinted buyers and sellers; no affected-user count disclosed

refund_route.value: Vinted provided clearer information on claiming a refund when a purchase does not arrive

counterfeit_route.value: Vinted provided more transparent information about counterfeit review and the steps needed to claim a refund

seller_identity.value: Vinted provided more detailed information about identity verification documents and information required from sellers

review_transparency.value: Vinted clarified how average ratings are calculated, the difference between automated and user-generated reviews, and how to report suspicious reviews

mechanism.value: Marketplace trust is a chain from purchase price to delivery, authenticity, seller identity, reputation signals, and reachable refund; improving one interface alone does not complete the chain

observations.method: European Commission summary of implemented Vinted website and app changes concerning buyer protection, counterfeits, identity verification, and reviews.
observations.uncertainty: The source records information and interface changes, not successful refund rates, counterfeit prevalence, dispute resolution time, seller compliance, or consumer comprehension.
observations.subgroup: EU/EEA Vinted buyers facing nondelivery or counterfeit goods and sellers undergoing identity or reputation processes.
observations.counterinterpretation: Clearer process information may shift effort to consumers, who still must recognize a problem, preserve evidence, and initiate the refund route.

observations.period: Vinted CPC follow-up; unresolved delivery-fee disclosure request

denominator.unit: EU/EEA Vinted purchase journeys with delivery options; no affected-journey count disclosed

unresolved_request.value: Vinted did not agree to inform consumers at the beginning of purchase that displayed prices exclude delivery fees or to show minimum delivery fees where available

possible_enforcement.value: The CPC Network urged Vinted to address the issue and may use enforcement measures if necessary

mechanism.value: A platform can implement most price and remedy controls while leaving a delivery-fee gap that preserves late-stage price uncertainty

observations.method: European Commission follow-up distinguishes Vinted changes already made from a delivery-fee disclosure request that remained unresolved.
observations.uncertainty: The source does not report whether further changes occurred after the stated follow-up, enforcement was initiated, or consumers experienced measurable savings or reduced abandonment.
observations.subgroup: EU/EEA Vinted consumers purchasing goods where delivery options and fees are selected later in checkout.
observations.counterinterpretation: Delivery fees can depend on seller, carrier, location, parcel size, and option, making early exact disclosure operationally difficult; that does not establish that consumers can compare the final price adequately.

related_sources.claim: The Viagogo factsheet provides a comparator in the same CPC environment where implementation monitoring remained explicit and some price/remedy requests were unresolved.
The Commission's marketplace and digital-services page reports Vinted's implemented controls and the remaining delivery-fee disclosure gap.

boundary: This record adds an EU/EEA second-hand marketplace implementation episode linking automatic fees, total-price disclosure, refund routes, counterfeit handling, seller identity, review transparency, and an unresolved delivery-fee gap. It does not quantify consumer harm, verify refund completion, estimate affordability or resale-market welfare, or prove that the controls changed behavior.
